introduction: Michigan’s Home Heating Credit helps qualifying homeowners and renters with heating expenses. The currently listed filing deadline was September 30, 2026.
description: Michigan’s Home Heating Credit helps qualifying homeowners and renters with heating expenses. The currently listed filing deadline was September 30, 2026.

sections.who: Eligibility depends on occupying a Michigan homestead, household resources and other filing conditions. Use the correct claim-year instructions.
sections.get: The credit helps with heating costs and may be issued through an energy draft or direct payment arrangements. It is not an immediate shutoff application.
sections.docs:
• Annual household-resource records, not just monthly income.
  • Heating-cost records for the specified claim period.
  • Lease or property information, especially where heat is included in rent.
sections.apply:
1. Check the claim year and deadline

    Review Treasury’s Home Heating Credit guidance. The listed September 30, 2026 deadline has passed.

  2. Use MI-1040CR-7

    The claim can be filed on its own if no MI-1040 return is required.

  3. Follow payment instructions

    If an energy draft cannot be used because heat is included in rent, follow Treasury’s review instructions.
sections.after: Check claim status through Treasury eServices. For a current emergency, contact MDHHS rather than waiting for the next credit cycle.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Home Heating Credit filing and payment guidance. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Can I file without a Michigan income-tax return?
Yes. MI-1040CR-7 can be submitted separately when no return is required.
Is the listed 2026 deadline still upcoming?
The instructions require annual household resources.
Use Treasury Individual Income Tax eServices.
